findings.description: The EC2 user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). These are stored in Terraform state and readable from instance metadata by anyone who can reach the instance, giving direct API access to the account.
The ingress rule opens TCP port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH to the entire internet and permitting brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the portal server.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true on subnet portal_subnet_a, so every instance launched there (including aws_instance.portal_server) receives a routable public IP and is directly reachable from the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true on subnet portal_subnet_b, forcing public IP addresses on all instances launched in that subnet and increasing internet-exposed attack surface.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so captured flow log data is stored unencrypted in S3.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket ACL is defined for the flow log bucket, so account-level or ACL-based public exposure of the archive is not prevented.
The EBS data volume for the portal server is created without encrypted = true, so the disk contents are stored unencrypted and are readable if the volume or a snapshot is exfiltrated.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and no encryption is specified, so the backup copies of the disk data are also stored in cleartext.
The egress rule allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, which permits a compromised instance to reach any external host for data exfiltration or command-and-control.
